messages.author: 232ec84ad2a445ea
messages.subject: recordTable on subset of directories
parts:
Hi,

I have a directory of nearly 1300 cameras across 3 years of a study (> 3 million images). I've previously run the recordTable function on camera stations for Years 1-2, which took days. Is there any way to restrict recordTable to only the Year 3 folders (designated by a '2021' in the folder name) to save processing time?

I've tried using a for loop to iterate over the folders, but I get a Error: inDir contains no station directories. Images are organized by camera, not species (i.e., Tagged/Camera1, Tagged/Camera2,...,Tagged/Camera1300).

Code sample:
Yr3cams <- list.files(path = "M:/data/CameraSampling/Tagged", pattern = "2021", full.names = TRUE, include.dirs = FALSE)

for (i in Yr3cams){
            recordTable(inDir = i, IDfrom  = "metadata",  timeZone = "EST",
            metadataspeciesTag = "Species", removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE,
            additionalMetadataTags = "EXIF:Flash", writecsv = TRUE)
}

Thanks for any advice!

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: recordTable on subset of directories
parts:
Hi,
currently that is not implemented, sorry. recordTable searches all subdirectories of inDir. I also never considered such an extreme case, and I am astonished the function ran for days (would have thought hours at most). 
Just to be sure I understand you correctly, you have one big folder (inDir) that contains data from 1300 cameras over 3 years, all side by side? So no subfolders for the different years? 

The Error: inDir contains no station directories.  is probably because the function expects station folders as subfolders of inDir, and gets confused if that's not the case (i.e., you can't replace inDir = "Tagged" with inDir = "Tagged/Camera1" because the station information will be lost. 

It should be easy to modify the function though. A few options:
1. "includeStation" argument
2.  "excludeStation" argument
3.  an argument like "stationDirs", which can optionally be used instead of inDir. 

Of course one could also combine the functionality of option 3 above with what "inDir" is doing already: 
if lenght(inDir) == 1 -> expect station subdirectories
if lenght(inDir) >= 2 -> consider each value in inDir as a station directory 

While possible, I think that would be confusing and inconsistent. 

What do you think would be best? Personally I favour option 1 (telling the function which stations you want). 

Alternatively, the low-tech solution would be to have separate directories for each year and just change inDir accordingly. 

Best,
Jürgen

That is correct, I have a single directory ("Tagged") containing ~1300 folders, each of which correspond to a unique camera set - it's a big study.  I'm copying the 2021 folders to their own directory to circumvent the issue but it's taking days (885 GB transferred so far, and that's only about halfway through).  In part I think the function takes so long because the directories are on a network drive rather than a local hard drive.

I think an "includeStation" argument would work great, particularly if you can feed it a list variable like my Yr3cams list above.

Cheers,
Pat

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: recordTable on subset of directories
parts:
Hi Pat,

sorry for the late reply. That is a huge study indeed, and it taking days to copy a few hundred Gb seems to suggest that the network drive may be a bottleneck indeed. Even at USB 2 speed it should only take a few hours to copy that amount of data, certainly not several days. If copying is that slow I suppose reading the data has the same problem. You can try with a local copy conting just a few stations and compare the time.

Please have a look at the attached script. It contains a modified version of recordTable which has an includeStation argument. First, source the attached file, then source the helper functions:

source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/master/R/variousOtherHelperFunctions.R")

Here's an example:

wd_images_ID_species <- system.file("pictures/sample_images_species_dir",
                                    package = "camtrapR")

rec_table1 <- recordTable(inDir               = wd_images_ID_species,
                          IDfrom                 = "directory", 
                          minDeltaTime           = 60,
                          deltaTimeComparedTo    = "lastRecord",
                          writecsv               = FALSE,
                          additionalMetadataTags = c("EXIF:Model", "EXIF:Make"),
                          includeStation         = c("StationB", "StationC")
)


It then only returns data for StationB and C, and doesn't scan StationA. Would you mind giving that a try and let me know how it went?

Thank you and best regards,

Jürgen

Thanks for the quick response! That is correct, I have a single directory ("Tagged") containing ~1300 folders, each of which correspond to a unique camera set - it's a big study.  I'm copying the 2021 folders to their own directory to circumvent the issue but it's taking days (885 GB transferred so far, and that's only about halfway through).  In part I think the function takes so long because the directories are on a network drive rather than a local hard drive.

I think an "includeStation" argument would work great, particularly if you can feed it a list variable like my Yr3cams list above.

Cheers,
Pat
